title: Universal primitive discriminant -23 multiplier cones at16,19,39

results.name: CN3MultiplierCones
results.scope: For every positive q with no inert prime factor and v23(q)<=1, the three numbers16q,19q,39q are each sums of two positive primitive x^2+xy+6y^2 numerical values. Inert-free q may have arbitrary split classes and exponents and need not itself be an ordinary or primitive principal norm.
consequences: Every target with inert part exactly19 and v23<=1 is represented, with arbitrary split multipliers.
Every inert-free target divisible by16 or39 and with v23<=1 is represented.
Every power of two at least16 is represented.
results.limits: No assertion for arbitrary inert factors in q, no complete40-exception classification and no historical-priority claim.

results.scope: For a specified finite list of positive{2,3,13}-smooth pairs with a common sum, the complete R0/R1 class-phase cover is equivalent to one of THOSE pairs giving two primitive norms after every multiplier q in the stated domain. R>=2 is automatic.

proof_dependencies.locator: Lemma CN3Individual and its explicit discriminant-23 specialization
proof_dependencies.scope: For inert-free n with v23(n)<=1, primitive principal representation holds exactly when the number of DISTINCT nonprincipal split prime powers with exponent nonzero mod3 is not one. Imports only this exact criterion and class-group specialization, not the analytic counts, profile asymptotics or Hecke estimates in other sections.
